latest_messages.headline: Pre-market: calm, healthy start to the week — no buys lined up (nothing cleared our bar). Deere's Thursday earnings is the week's key event.
latest_messages.body: Ran the full 4-analyst team before the open; no trades (market closed). Our three stocks are all fine: JPMorgan got another price-target bump (Wells Fargo to $390), Eli Lilly is quiet with a competitor actually downgraded because Lilly is winning the weight-loss-pill race. No new stock cleared our strict checklist - the one I looked hardest at, Eaton (a power-grid/data-center name), is up too far too fast to chase safely, so it stays benched. No big economic report today; the Fed's Jackson Hole meeting is next week, not this one. The main event: Deere reports earnings Thursday Aug 20 - I'll decide Mon/Tue whether to hold through it or trim first, and won't add beforehand. We're at $101,333 (+1.3% since our $100K start), ~36% cash - room for one good buy when a real one shows up.

latest_messages.headline: Week ending Aug 14: -0.33% | SPY +0.41% | alpha -0.73% | grade C — we still trailed the market, but the month-long cash-drag problem got FIXED this week and it worked.
latest_messages.body: Book -0.33% vs SPY +0.41% (behind ~0.73 pts); cumulative alpha now -1.10. But the story is the fix: I built the S&P 500 'floor' Mon/Tue (the Option B you approved) and it tracked the index almost exactly (+0.44% vs +0.41%), cutting cash from ~75% to ~36%. For four weeks the miss was cash drag; this week it wasn't - the small lag was two of our own names, Deere (-2.0% into its Aug 20 earnings) and Eli Lilly (-2.4% since Wed's re-entry), both theses intact. JPM +10% and beat the market again. No strategy change - the right move is to let the just-live fix prove itself, not tweak off one small stock-specific miss. Watching Deere's Aug 20 earnings (hold-through vs trim decision Mon/Tue) and Lilly steadying. +1.38% since our $100K start; ~36% cash. Grade C, up from D - beat SPY on the next up-week and it's a B.
